title: Stone Soup
strapline: A soup made from a stone — and a little something from everyone.
intent: A story about a whole village sharing a little each teaches generosity, community and how much we make when we all contribute.
Building the soup ingredient by ingredient sequences a process and names real vegetables and foods.
Making a real soup together ties the tale to cooking, tasting, change through heat and sharing a meal.
The clever traveller who gets everyone to give opens gentle talk about kindness, sharing and welcome.
The cooking pot becomes a small world for gathering, adding, stirring and sharing.
implementation: Set out a big pot, a special stone and lots of pretend or real vegetables for children to add to the soup.
Tell the story so the soup grows richer as each villager gives, then let children play out the sharing.
Make a real soup together — chopping, adding, stirring, smelling and tasting — with everyone contributing something.
Sequence the cooking: 'What shall we add next? What has to go in before it tastes good?'
Draw out the message warmly: 'Everyone gave just a little, and look how much soup we made together.'
Follow the play — some children will cook and share for the whole room, others will retell the giving.
key_questions: What could we add to make the soup even better?
How did a soup made from a stone feed the whole village?
What happens to the vegetables as the soup cooks?
How did everyone helping make such a difference?
Who shall we share our soup with?

impact.text: Children add ingredients in sequence and name real vegetables and foods.
Children make and taste a real soup and notice the vegetables changing as they cook.
Children talk about sharing, giving and community.
Children show kindness and share what they make with others.
Children act out the gathering and sharing with roles and shared ideas.

enhancements: A real soup-making session where every child brings or chops one ingredient to add.
A big cooking-pot role-play with a special soup stone and baskets of vegetables.
A vegetable-naming and sorting tray to build food vocabulary.
A 'we all gave a little' display showing what each child contributed.
A sharing table to serve the finished soup to the room or to families.

playing_exploring: Children chop, add, stir and taste, exploring the whole soup-making with their senses.
They play the village, each adding their own ingredient to the pot.
active_learning: Children see the soup through from stone to shared bowl.
They persist with chopping and stirring for the reward of the meal.
creating_thinking: Children reason about what to add and in what order.
They grasp how everyone giving a little makes a lot, and talk about it.
